notes.body:
added 3 commits
  • 9a1c2c80...9fb22c1e - 2 commits from branch wireshark:master
  • e51b08a3 - Linux: rename metadata according to spec
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/1153/diffs?diff_id=129150428&start_sha=9a1c2c804202376a551a382317c7fa8a2c250ae8)

  • 9a46fabf - 1 commit from branch wireshark:master
  • 42a09ad0 - Linux: rename metadata according to spec
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/1153/diffs?diff_id=130156001&start_sha=b6964b02b521cf912ef7a1e1749bb55ae0fdb893)
enabled an automatic merge when the pipeline for 42a09ad02e7f51707927230ecd124938462d18c0 succeeds
@guyharris No idea how your change to the topic got lost during apply.

This is an enormously wonderful feature of GitLab.

If you create a merge request for a commit, the merge request's comment is a *copy* of the commit message; changing one does not change the other.

I've had to update merge requests when I changed the commit message.
It looks like this broke RPM packaging, e.g. https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/jobs/903765081.
@eszlari Can you take a look at this?
